The Incident Between Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and his Son Concerning the Criminals of Damascus

Hadhrat Bilaal bin Sa'd Ash'ari narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) to submit to him the names of all the criminals of Damascus. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "What have I to do with the criminals of Damascus? How am I to know who they are?" His son Bilaal then offered to write their names and when he did, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "How do you know them? You would never know that they are criminals unless you are amongst them, so begin with your own name." He then did not send the list.[^2]
The Incident Between Hadhrat Jareer (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was once in a room with Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah (RA) (and others) when he smelt an odour (from someone who had passed wind). Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I command the person responsible for this odour to get up and perform wudhu." Hadhrat Jareer (RA) then said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Should everyone rather not perform wudhu (so that the one person is not embarrassed)?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) praised him saying, "You were an excellent leader during the Period of Ignorance and now an excellent guide in Islaam."[^3]

The Letter of Hadhrat Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA)

Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched him, Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Miqdaad (RA) with instruction saying, "Ride until you reach Rawda Khaakh[^4] There you will find a woman in her carriage with a note that you should take from her."
The Sahabah (RA) raced their horses to the place where they saw the woman. When they asked here for the note, she denied having it in her possession. When they threatened to remove all her clothing if she did not surrender the note, she removed the note from the plait of her hair. When they brought the note to Rasulullaah ﷺ, they discovered that it was from Hadhrat Haatib bin Abi Balta'ah (RA) and it was addressed to the Mushrikeen of Makkah, passing on to them some information about (the intentions of) Rasulullaah ﷺ.
